### Space groups

(eb-42)=
#### EB-42 · A space group is a short name plus a setting code

{bdg-success}`handled` · easydiffraction 0.21.1

**easydiffraction does:** easydiffraction takes one of 230 short names and a separate setting code: 531 settings in all.

**PowderLine does:** The easydiffraction gateway translates the canonical name into a short name and a setting code. It refuses what easydiffraction cannot express.

**You see:** validation error

(eb-80)=
#### EB-80 · Each calculator misreads some settings

{bdg-success}`handled` · easydiffraction 0.21.1 (CrysPy 0.13.0, CrysFML 0.8.0)

**easydiffraction does:** CrysFML is handed the short symbol alone. It misreads almost every non-default setting: unique axis, cell choice, `:R` and some origin-1 groups. CrysPy computes 41 settings as another setting: most c- and a-unique monoclinic settings, the `:R` settings, some origin-1 settings, and `P 31`, which it computes with the operators of `P 32`.

**PowderLine does:** Validation accepts, per calculator, only the settings whose computation passed for a general position and for every special site: 428 of the 531 for CrysPy, 230 for CrysFML. The error names a setting of the same group that the calculator computes, or the other calculator.

**You see:** validation error

(eb-84)=
#### EB-84 · CrysPy crashes on 53 settings

{bdg-success}`handled` · easydiffraction 0.21.1 (CrysPy 0.13.0)

**easydiffraction does:** CrysPy crashes on 53 settings: 51 cell-choice settings such as `A 1 2 1` and `I 1 2 1`, plus `P 6/m` and `F d -3 c:2`. CrysFML runs them.

**PowderLine does:** Validation refuses these settings for the cryspy calculator ({ref}`EB-80 <eb-80>`). The error names a setting of the same group that CrysPy computes, or the crysfml calculator.

**You see:** validation error

(eb-83)=
#### EB-83 · CrysPy resets the unique angle of some monoclinic cells to 90°

{bdg-success}`handled` · easydiffraction 0.21.1 (CrysPy 0.13.0)

**easydiffraction does:** For c-unique and a-unique monoclinic cells, CrysPy resets the unique angle to 90°.

**PowderLine does:** These settings are not among those validation accepts for the cryspy calculator. The error names a setting of the same group that CrysPy computes, or the crysfml calculator.

### Special positions and sites

(eb-12)=
#### EB-12 · CrysPy rationalizes and snaps coordinates

{bdg-success}`handled` · easydiffraction 0.21.1 (CrysPy 0.13.0)

**easydiffraction does:** CrysPy rationalizes each coordinate to a denominator of at most 10⁵. It snaps 5-decimal thirds.

**PowderLine does:** Core hands over exact values, so CrysPy's own tolerance never matters.

(eb-47)=
#### EB-47 · easydiffraction applies site symmetry itself

{bdg-success}`handled` · easydiffraction 0.21.1

**easydiffraction does:** easydiffraction detects each atom's Wyckoff position and marks the coordinates and Uij fixed by symmetry. It ignores a `free` flag on them, and coupled coordinates follow the free one. A user edit of a value re-detects the Wyckoff position with tolerance 1e-3, so an off-special coordinate can change the multiplicity.

**PowderLine does:** The gateway hands over core's exact values. After the build, it checks easydiffraction's multiplicity and coordinates against core's for every atom. A mismatch stops the run before refining, with reason `unusable_site`, and names the atom.

**You see:** `unusable_site`

(eb-74)=
#### EB-74 · Wyckoff positions are detected when the structure is built, never during a fit

{bdg-success}`handled` · easydiffraction 0.21.1

**easydiffraction does:** easydiffraction detects Wyckoff positions when a structure is built and when a user edit moves a coordinate. An edit within the 1e-3 tolerance rewrites the stored value (x = 0.4995 becomes 0.5). During a fit nothing is re-detected, so a refined coordinate drifting toward a special position is never snapped. A position written as another lattice translation of the template's pattern is stored in easydiffraction's own writing.

**PowderLine does:** The gateway hands over core's exact values, and core's 5e-6 to 2e-3 band refuses every position the detection could move. A position stored translated by a lattice vector is the same atom: it is accepted with a warning, and reports keep the recipe's writing. A refined coordinate that ends near a special position is reported through the output recipe ({ref}`KI-18 <ki-18>`).

**You see:** `easydiffraction_position_translated`, `output_recipe_not_valid`

(eb-77)=
#### EB-77 · CrysPy computes some special positions wrongly

{bdg-success}`handled` · easydiffraction 0.21.1 (CrysPy 0.13.0)

**easydiffraction does:** CrysPy computes wrong structure factors for some equivalent writings of a special position with a free coordinate. LaB6's B written as (½, ½, x) instead of the template's (x, ½, ½) gives intensities off by up to ×2. It also computes special positions wrongly in nine origin-choice-1 settings. General positions and fixed special positions are right.

**PowderLine does:** With `calculator: "cryspy"`, an atom on such a site must be written in the pattern of easydiffraction's Wyckoff template. Otherwise the run stops before refining, with reason `unusable_site`, and names the position to write. `--validate-only` does not catch this. The nine settings are refused at validation for the cryspy calculator. CrysFML has no such rule.

**You see:** `unusable_site`, validation error

### Cell, ADPs and occupancy

(eb-23)=
#### EB-23 · CrysFML ignores anisotropic ADPs

{bdg-success}`handled` · easydiffraction 0.21.1 (CrysFML 0.8.0)

**easydiffraction does:** easydiffraction supports anisotropic ADPs, but CrysFML is handed only B = 8π²·Ueq. A `Uaniso` has no effect with CrysFML.

**PowderLine does:** `Uaniso` with the crysfml calculator is a validation error.

**You see:** validation error

(eb-86)=
#### EB-86 · A refined Uij can land in the wrong atom's column

{bdg-success}`handled` · easydiffraction 0.21.1 (CrysPy 0.13.0)

**easydiffraction does:** With CrysPy, easydiffraction writes a refined Uij into the wrong atom's column whenever an isotropic atom precedes the anisotropic one. The refined tensor then has no effect.

**PowderLine does:** The gateway hands the anisotropic atoms to easydiffraction first. Reports keep the recipe's order. A test proves that a refined Uij moves.

(eb-46)=
#### EB-46 · Negative ADPs are refused at input

{bdg-success}`handled` · easydiffraction 0.21.1

**easydiffraction does:** easydiffraction refuses a negative `Uiso` or U11, U22, U33 at input. Its physical limit for them is 0–10 Å². The minimizer skips that check, so a refinement can still carry a negative value, and the pattern stays finite.

**PowderLine does:** An `easydiffraction.*` recipe may not state a negative `Uiso` or U11, U22, U33: validation error.

**You see:** validation error

(eb-22)=
#### EB-22 · Occupancy outside [0, 1] is refused

{bdg-success}`handled` · easydiffraction 0.21.1

**easydiffraction does:** easydiffraction refuses an occupancy outside [0, 1].

**PowderLine does:** Core requires 0 ≤ occupancy ≤ 1 for every engine, so the recipe is refused before easydiffraction sees it.

**You see:** validation error

### Bounds and limits

(eb-71)=
#### EB-71 · Unbounded sides get physical limits, and starts are moved silently

{bdg-success}`handled` · easydiffraction 0.21.1

**easydiffraction does:** When a fit starts, easydiffraction gives an unbounded side its physical limit: cell lengths 0–30 Å, angles 0–180°, occupancy 0–1, `adp_iso` and U11/U22/U33 0–10 Å², scale, wavelength and μR ≥ 0. It refuses a value outside a physical limit at input, even when fixed, so no cell over 30 Å can be modeled. lmfit moves a start outside its bounds onto the bound without a message.

**PowderLine does:** A stated bound replaces the physical limit on its side, and `null` keeps it. A value outside a physical limit is a validation error. A refined value that ends within 1e-6 (relative) of a bound or physical limit gets a warning. For a limit of 0, the test is within 1e-6 of the starting value.

**You see:** validation error, `easydiffraction_parameter_at_limit`

### Peak profile and instrument

(eb-75)=
#### EB-75 · The X-ray corrections easydiffraction models, and its polarization

{bdg-success}`handled` · easydiffraction 0.21.1 (CrysPy 0.13.0, CrysFML 0.8.0)

**easydiffraction does:** Both calculators model the Kα doublet, the Lorentz factor and the polarization factor 1 − p + p cos²2θ_m cos²2θ, the 2θ offset, sample displacement and transparency, and Hewat cylinder absorption. A second wavelength alone does nothing. 2θ_m acts only with p > 0. GSAS-II's polarization P is easydiffraction's 1 − p: copying P to p is a 6.6 % intensity error at 15° 2θ.

**PowderLine does:** Every correction is a recipe slot; left out means not modeled. The schema requires both Kα2 fields or neither. The hand-derived per-engine recipes state p = 1 − P.

**You see:** validation error

(eb-87)=
#### EB-87 · Negative peak widths give a wrong pattern without a message

{bdg-success}`handled` · easydiffraction 0.21.1 (CrysPy 0.13.0, CrysFML 0.8.0)

**easydiffraction does:** Where U tan²θ + V tanθ + W < 0, CrysFML drops the peaks and CrysPy distorts them. Where X tanθ + Y/cosθ < 0, both give a finite pattern 12–24 % off.

**PowderLine does:** A stated profile that makes a width negative is a validation error. The check covers the handed points and a 0.01° grid over the window widened by 1° plus the position corrections. A refined profile that does so gets a warning. In `example_LaB6_ionic`, the CrysPy pseudo-Voigt fit refines X to −0.097, so the Lorentzian width is negative from about 11.3° on.

**You see:** validation error, `easydiffraction_negative_width`

**Seen in:** `example_LaB6_ionic`

### Preferred orientation

(eb-97)=
#### EB-97 · Preferred orientation reaches CrysPy only, under the right key

{bdg-success}`handled` · easydiffraction 0.21.1 (CrysPy 0.13.0, CrysFML 0.8.0)

**easydiffraction does:** Only the CrysPy calculator reads the experiment's preferred-orientation rows. CrysFML's pattern does not change with `march_r`, without a message. CrysPy also ignores a row whose `structure_id` is not the lowercase linked structure name, silently.

**PowderLine does:** `preferred_orientation` with `calculator: "crysfml"` is a validation error. The builder keys the row by the structure name easydiffraction uses.

**You see:** validation error

(eb-98)=
#### EB-98 · CrysPy's March correction is Dollase's times r^1.5

{bdg-secondary}`documented` · easydiffraction 0.21.1 (CrysPy 0.13.0)

**easydiffraction does:** CrysPy's texture correction is not volume-normalized, so every textured-to-untextured intensity ratio carries the constant r^1.5. With `march_random_fract` = 0 the scale absorbs it, and the refined `march_r` is the same r as GSAS-II's. With f > 0 the correction is (1 − f)·r^1.5·A + f, and the refined r and f are not GSAS-II's quantities.

**PowderLine does:** Documented. A test compares normalized ratios with GSAS-II's March–Dollase correction.

### Data and the fit window

(eb-70)=
#### EB-70 · Only the handed points are calculated

{bdg-secondary}`documented` · easydiffraction 0.21.1

**easydiffraction does:** easydiffraction calculates only the points it is handed, and maps its Chebyshev basis over them. Reflection tails from beyond the window are lost: at most 3e-4 σ at the refined scale.

**PowderLine does:** The gateway hands easydiffraction exactly the weighted points inside the window, so it fits the points core scores. The lost tails are documented.

**PowderLine does:** Weights above 1e8 on handed points are a validation error.

### Calculators

(eb-76)=
#### EB-76 · The two calculators compute different peak types

{bdg-success}`handled` · easydiffraction 0.21.1 (CrysPy 0.13.0, CrysFML 0.8.0)

**easydiffraction does:** CrysPy computes `cwl-pseudo-voigt` and the Bérar–Baldinozzi empirical asymmetry. CrysFML computes `cwl-pseudo-voigt` and the Thompson–Cox–Hastings profile with FCJ axial asymmetry. Both pseudo-Voigts are the TCH pseudo-Voigt with Caglioti Gaussian and X tanθ + Y/cosθ Lorentzian widths. `cutoff_fwhm` acts in CrysPy only; CrysFML uses a fixed 30-FWHM window.

**PowderLine does:** The peak type must be one the chosen calculator computes. Otherwise validation fails.

**You see:** validation error

(eb-79)=
#### EB-79 · CrysFML reports no reflection list

{bdg-warning}`warned` · easydiffraction 0.21.1 (CrysFML 0.8.0)

**easydiffraction does:** CrysFML reports no reflection list.

**PowderLine does:** No peak list reports are written with CrysFML, and the result says so.

**You see:** `easydiffraction_reflections_not_available`

(eb-90)=
#### EB-90 · CrysFML refinements depend on their starting values

{bdg-warning}`warned` · easydiffraction 0.21.1 (CrysFML 0.8.0)

**easydiffraction does:** CrysFML computes in single precision, below lmfit's finite-difference step. A CrysFML refinement stops at a point that depends on its starting values. Starts changed by 1e-6 (relative) gave Rwp 6.79 % against 6.27 %, with cells stable to about 1e-5.

**PowderLine does:** Every CrysFML refinement carries a warning. The calculator stays available because you choose it, and PowderLine states the difference.

**You see:** `easydiffraction_crysfml_start_dependent`

(eb-78)=
#### EB-78 · CrysFML's integrated intensities drift with angle

{bdg-secondary}`documented` · easydiffraction 0.21.1 (CrysFML 0.8.0)

**easydiffraction does:** Relative to m·|F|²·Lorentz, CrysFML's integrated intensities drift by −4 % from 3° to 15° 2θ. This biases `Uiso` by about +0.001 Å².

**PowderLine does:** The calculator is recorded in every result.

(eb-93)=
#### EB-93 · On the temperature series, easydiffraction refines La's Uiso low

{bdg-secondary}`documented` · easydiffraction 0.21.1 (CrysPy 0.13.0, CrysFML 0.8.0)

**easydiffraction does:** On GSAS-II-calculated LaB6 patterns, easydiffraction refines La's Uiso 10–22 % low. B's Uiso, the thermal expansion and GoF ≈ 1 agree. The cause is the series' profile: GSAS-II clamps its Lorentzian width to 0.001 centideg above about 10.7°, so the high-angle peaks are pure Gaussian. Neither a symmetric pseudo-Voigt nor TCH can represent that, and `Uiso` absorbs the mismatch. Simulated with a profile easydiffraction can represent, CrysPy's La Uiso is 0.00863 against 0.00858 programmed. CrysFML's is 0.00823 (−4 %), the size of its intensity drift ({ref}`EB-78 <eb-78>`).

**PowderLine does:** Documented, no code change. Across engines, compare cells, with the {ref}`EB-88 <eb-88>`-size offsets in mind, and the expansion. Absolute `Uiso` agrees only when the profile models agree.

**Seen in:** `example_LaB6_temperature_series`

{bdg-success}`handled` · easydiffraction 0.21.1

{bdg-secondary}`documented` · easydiffraction 0.21.1
